   120	    Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange L).sheaf = 1 := by
   121	  set P : (relCurve C L).MeromorphicPresentation :=
   122	    Scheme.MeromorphicPresentation.ofCocycle (D.baseChange L).pointedCover
   123	      (gluedSubordCocycle (D.baseChange L).isGluingCocycle
   124	        (D.baseChange L).pointedCover (D.baseChange L).pieceIndex
   125	        fun _ => le_rfl) with hP
   126	  have hsubP : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (P.gluedSheaf L) 1) :=
   127	    (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv (presentationSheafIso (D.baseChange L)) 1).toEquiv.subsingleton_congr.mp
   128	      hsub
   129	  have h0eq : Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange L).sheaf = Sheaf.h0 (P.gluedSheaf L) :=
   130	    Sheaf.h0_congr (presentationSheafIso (D.baseChange L))
   131	  have hformula := h0_gluedSheaf_eq_classDeg_add_chi L P hsubP
   132	  have hPclass : P.picClass = (D.baseChange L).cechPicClass := rfl
   133	  have hint : (Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange L).sheaf : ℤ) = 1 := by
   134	    rw [h0eq, hformula, hPclass, hg, chi_relCurve hχ L]; ring
   135	  exact_mod_cast hint
   136	
   137	/-! ## Σ-RANK1: the rank-1 export on the vanishing locus -/
   138	
   139	/-- **Σ-RANK1, the datum-level rank export** (worksheet GAP-3): on the fibrewise
   140	h¹-vanishing locus, at fibre degree `n` with the base χ-normalization `χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n`,
   141	the datum engine's `H⁰` has stalk-rank exactly `1` at `p`.
   142	
   143	`Module.rankAtStalk_eq` reads the rank as the `κ(p)`-dimension of the fibre
   144	`κ(p) ⊗[S] H⁰`; the on-the-nose base change `datumH0BaseChange` identifies this fibre with
   145	`H⁰(C_{κ(p)}, F_{D_{κ(p)}})`, whose dimension is `1` by the fibre computation. The global
   146	fibrewise hypothesis `hfib` supplies finiteness/projectivity (hence flatness) through
   147	`datumRigidEngine`. -/
   148	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one
   149	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C S π) [IsNoetherianRing S]
   150	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   151	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
   152	    (hfib : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S,
   153	      Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[S] q.asIdeal.ResidueField))
   154	    (p : PrimeSpectrum S)
   155	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField)]
   156	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   157	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   158	    [QuasiCompact
   159	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   160	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   161	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0)]
   162	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   163	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1)]
   164	    (hg : classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   165	      (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = (n : ℤ)) :
   166	    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
   167	  obtain ⟨-, hfin, hproj⟩ := datumRigidEngine D hπ hfib
   168	  haveI := hfin
   169	  haveI := hproj
   170	  have hH1 : Subsingleton (datumPair D).H1 := datum_subsingleton_pairH1 D hπ hfib
   171	  have hfibre : Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf = 1 :=
   172	    D.h0_sheaf_baseChange_eq_one hχ p.asIdeal.ResidueField hg
   173	      (D.datum_subsingleton_h1_baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField hH1)
   174	  calc Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p
   175	      = Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   176	          (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[S] (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0)) :=
   177	        Module.rankAtStalk_eq p
   178	    _ = Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   179	          (Sheaf.HModule (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf 0) :=
   180	        (D.datumH0BaseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField hH1).finrank_eq
   181	    _ = Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf := rfl
   182	    _ = 1 := hfibre
   183	
   184	/-! ## The certified-family specialization: N1 (invertible `H⁰`) and N3 (generators) -/
   185	
   186	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
   187	/-- (Implementation) The fibre class of the divisor datum has `classDeg = n` at `κ(p)`:
   188	the base change of `G.eqns`, read through `DivFamZar.classDeg_picClass`. -/
   189	private theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.classDeg_baseChange_divisorDatum
   190	    (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C S π n) (p : PrimeSpectrum S)
   191	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField)]
   192	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   193	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   194	    [QuasiCompact
   195	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   196	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   197	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0)]
   198	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   199	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1)] :
   200	    classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   201	      (G.adaptation.divisorDatum.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = (n : ℤ) := by
   202	  have hcl : G.adaptation.divisorDatum.cechPicClass = (DivFam.mk G).toZar.picClass := by
   203	    rw [G.adaptation.cechPicClass_divisorDatum, DivFamZar.picClass_toZar, DivFam.picClass_mk]
   204	  rw [G.adaptation.divisorDatum.cechPicClass_baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField, hcl,
   205	    ← DivFamZar.picClass_mapAlg]
   206	  exact DivFamZar.classDeg_picClass
   207	    (DivFamZar.mapAlg p.asIdeal.ResidueField n (DivFam.mk G).toZar)
   208	
   209	/-- **N1 — invertibility of the canonical `H⁰`** (worksheet §2 (N1)): for a certified
   210	divisor family `G` landing in the h¹-vanishing locus `V` (`hvan`), the divisor datum
   211	`D_G := G.adaptation.divisorDatum` has `H⁰` of stalk-rank exactly `1` at every prime.
   212	
   213	The fibre-degree hypothesis of `rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one` is discharged uniformly:
   214	the fibre class of `D_G` at `κ(p)` is the base change of `G.eqns`, which has
   215	`classDeg = n` at every field (`DivFamZar.classDeg_picClass`). -/
   216	theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.rankAtStalk_divisorDatum_eq_one
   217	    (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C S π n) [IsNoetherianRing S]
   218	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   219	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
   220	    (hvan : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum S, (DivFam.mk G).toZar.IsH1VanishingAt p)
   221	    (p : PrimeSpectrum S) :
   222	    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
   223	  have hfib : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S,
   224	      Subsingleton ((datumPair G.adaptation.divisorDatum).H1 ⊗[S] q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   225	    fun q => (G.isH1VanishingAt_toZar_iff q).mp (hvan q)
   226	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   227	    instIsIntegralBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   228	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   229	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   230	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   231	  haveI : QuasiCompact
   232	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   233	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   234	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   235	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0) :=
   236	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   237	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   238	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1) :=
   239	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   240	  exact G.adaptation.divisorDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one hπ hχ hfib p
   241	    (G.classDeg_baseChange_divisorDatum p)
   242	
   243	/-- **N3 — the generator kit** (worksheet §2 (N3)): since `H⁰(F_{D_G})` is projective of
   244	stalk-rank `1` on the locus, its `κ(p)`-fibre is nontrivial, so a fibrewise-nonzero
   245	**global** section exists on a basic open `D(f) ∋ p` — the Zariski-local generator
   246	(`Module.exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective`, the Nakayama-neighbourhood kit of
   247	`Picard/LocalGenerators.lean`). -/
   248	theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.exists_fibrewise_generator_divisorDatum
   249	    (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C S π n) [IsNoetherianRing S]
   250	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   251	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
   252	    (hvan : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum S, (DivFam.mk G).toZar.IsH1VanishingAt p)
   253	    (p : PrimeSpectrum S) :
   254	    ∃ f : S, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ ∃ q : Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0,
   255	      ∀ q' : PrimeSpectrum S, f ∉ q'.asIdeal →
   256	        (q ⊗ₜ (1 : q'.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   257	            Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0 ⊗[S] q'.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0 := by
   258	  have hfib : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S,
   259	      Subsingleton ((datumPair G.adaptation.divisorDatum).H1 ⊗[S] q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   260	    fun q => (G.isH1VanishingAt_toZar_iff q).mp (hvan q)
   261	  obtain ⟨-, hfin, hproj⟩ := datumRigidEngine G.adaptation.divisorDatum hπ hfib
   262	  haveI := hfin
   263	  haveI := hproj
   264	  have hrank : Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) p = 1 :=
   265	    G.rankAtStalk_divisorDatum_eq_one hπ hχ hvan p
   266	  -- rank 1 ⟹ the `κ(p)`-fibre is nontrivial
   267	  have hfr : Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   268	      (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[S] Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) = 1 := by
   269	    rw [← Module.rankAtStalk_eq]; exact hrank
   270	  haveI : Nontrivial (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[S]
   271	      Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) :=
   272	    Module.nontrivial_of_finrank_pos (by rw [hfr]; norm_num)
   273	  have hnt : Nontrivial (Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0 ⊗[S]
   274	      p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   275	    (TensorProduct.comm S _ _).toEquiv.symm.nontrivial
   276	  exact Module.exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective p hnt
   277

     9	/-!
    10	# Restricting a scheme module to the base ring
    11	
    12	For a scheme `X` over `Spec k`, this file views an `X.Modules` object as a sheaf of
    13	`k`-modules.  The construction keeps the same section types and restriction maps; only the
    14	scalar action is restricted along `k -> Gamma(X, U)`.  It is the dialect bridge needed to
    15	compare a `Scheme.Modules` line bundle with the fixed-base module sheaves used by the Cech
    16	cohomology engine.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	set_option autoImplicit false
    20	
    21	universe u
    22	
    23	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
    24	
    25	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
    26	
    27	variable {k : Type u} [CommRing k]
    28	
    29	/-- The base-ring module structure on sections of a scheme module. -/
    30	@[reducible] noncomputable def moduleKSections
    31	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : X.left.Modules)
    32	    (U : X.left.Opens) : Module k Γ(M, U) :=
    33	  Module.compHom _ (X.left.overAlgebraMap k U)
    34	
    35	attribute [local instance] moduleKSections
    36	
    37	/-- The native structure-sheaf action, with section-notation binders kept explicit. -/
    38	private noncomputable def smulSection
    39	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : X.left.Modules)
    40	    (U : X.left.Opens) (r : Γ(X.left, U)) (x : Γ(M, U)) : Γ(M, U) :=
    41	  r • x
    42	
    43	/-- The presheaf underlying a scheme module after restriction of scalars to the base ring. -/
    44	noncomputable def toModuleKPresheafOfModules
    45	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : X.left.Modules) :
    46	    X.left.Opensᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} k where
    47	  obj U := ModuleCat.of k Γ(M, U.unop)
    48	  map {U V} f := ModuleCat.ofHom
    49	    { toFun := fun x => M.presheaf.map f x
    50	      map_add' := fun x y => map_add _ x y
    51	      map_smul' := fun r x =>
    52	        (Scheme.Modules.map_smul M f.unop (X.left.overAlgebraMap k U.unop r) x).trans
    53	          (congrArg
    54	            (fun (s : Γ(X.left, V.unop)) =>
    55	              smulSection X M V.unop s (M.presheaf.map f x))
    56	            (X.left.overAlgebraMap_apply_res k f r)) }
    57	  map_id U := by
    58	    ext x
    59	    exact congrFun (congrArg (fun (f : M.presheaf.obj U ⟶ M.presheaf.obj U) =>
    60	      (ConcreteCategory.hom f : _ → _)) (M.presheaf.map_id U)) x
    61	  map_comp {U V W} f g := by
    62	    ext x
    63	    exact congrFun (congrArg (fun (h : M.presheaf.obj U ⟶ M.presheaf.obj W) =>
    64	      (ConcreteCategory.hom h : _ → _)) (M.presheaf.map_comp f g)) x
    65	
    66	/-- The restricted presheaf is a sheaf because its underlying additive presheaf is unchanged. -/
    67	lemma toModuleKPresheafOfModules_isSheaf
    68	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : X.left.Modules) :
    69	    Presheaf.IsSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.left.toTopCat)
    70	      (toModuleKPresheafOfModules X M) := by
    71	  rw [Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget _ _ (CategoryTheory.forget (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
    72	  convert (Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget _ _
    73	      (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u})).mp (Scheme.Modules.isSheaf M) using 1 <;> rfl
    74	
    75	/-- A sheaf of `O_X`-modules, viewed as a sheaf of modules over the base ring. -/
    76	noncomputable def toModuleKSheafOfModules
    77	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : X.left.Modules) :
    78	    Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k) :=
    79	  ⟨toModuleKPresheafOfModules X M, toModuleKPresheafOfModules_isSheaf X M⟩
    80	
    81	/-- Restriction maps of the base-ring sheaf are definitionally those of the scheme module. -/
    82	lemma toModuleKSheafOfModules_obj_map_apply
    83	    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (M : X.left.Modules)
    84	    {V W : X.left.Opens} (h : W ≤ V)
    85	    (x : (toModuleKSheafOfModules X M).obj.obj (op V)) :
    86	    ((toModuleKSheafOfModules X M).obj.map (homOfLE h).op).hom x =
    87	      M.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op x :=
    88	  rfl
    89	
    90	namespace Modules
    91	
    92	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
    93	
    94	/-- A scheme module which is locally isomorphic to the structure sheaf. -/
    95	def IsLineBundle (M : X.Modules) : Prop :=
    96	  ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧
    97	    Nonempty ((restrictFunctor U.ι).obj M ≅ SheafOfModules.unit U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf)
    98	
    99	end Modules
   100	
   101	end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

   121	/-- The restricted chart-0 pieces cover the overlap of the pinned charts (the
   122	partition witness restricts to a partition witness). -/
   123	lemma coverInf : (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓ (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁
   124	    ≤ ⨆ j : D.J₀, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (D.hInf j) := by
   125	  refine le_iSup_basicOpen_of_sum_eq_one
   126	    (fun j => (relCurve C B).resHom inf_le_left (D.a₀ j)) D.hInf ?_
   127	  have hres := congrArg
   128	    ((relCurve C B).resHom (inf_le_left : (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓
   129	      (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ ≤ (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀))
   130	    D.partition₀
   131	  rw [map_sum, map_one] at hres
   132	  rw [← hres]
   133	  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => (map_mul _ _ _).symm
   134	
   135	end BasicOpenCoverData
   136	
   137	/-- **The pinned cocycle datum over `B`** (worksheet §3.2, VERBATIM): the basic-open
   138	cover data of the two pinned charts together with transition units on the pairwise
   139	basic-open overlaps (with explicit inverse witnesses — `Units`) satisfying the cocycle
   140	identities in the overlap section rings (`Scheme.IsGluingCocycle`, including the
   141	normalization `g j j = 1`). This is the DAT-1 constructor input and the object RE-5
   142	descends. -/
   143	structure BasicOpenCocycleDatum [IsAffineHom π] : Type (u + 1) extends
   144	    BasicOpenCoverData C B π where
   145	  /-- The transition units on the pairwise piece overlaps. -/
   146	  unit : ∀ i j : toBasicOpenCoverData.index,
   147	    Γ(relCurve C B, toBasicOpenCoverData.pieces i ⊓ toBasicOpenCoverData.pieces j)ˣ
   148	  /-- The cocycle law. -/
   149	  isGluingCocycle : Scheme.IsGluingCocycle toBasicOpenCoverData.pieces unit
   150	
   151	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
   152	
   153	variable {C B π} [IsAffineHom π] (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
   154	
   155	/-- **The glued sheaf of the datum**: the m-chart cocycle-glued sheaf of `B`-modules on
   156	the small Zariski site of the relative curve `C_B`. -/
   157	@[reducible] noncomputable def sheaf :
   158	    Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((relCurve C B : Scheme.{u}) : TopCat))
   159	      (ModuleCat.{u} B) :=
   160	  gluedSheaf B D.pieces D.unit
   161	
   162	/-- The quasi-coherence packaging of the datum's glued sheaf on the pinned chart
   163	`V₀ᴮ`, from the chart-0 family. -/
   164	noncomputable instance instQcohOn₀ :
   165	    Scheme.QcohOn D.sheaf (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ :=
   166	  gluedQcohOn B D.pieces D.unit D.isGluingCocycle (σ := Sum.inl) (h := D.h₀)
   167	    (fun _ => le_rfl) D.cover₀
   168	
   169	/-- The quasi-coherence packaging on the pinned chart `V₁ᴮ`, from the chart-1
   170	family. -/
   171	noncomputable instance instQcohOn₁ :
   172	    Scheme.QcohOn D.sheaf (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ :=
   173	  gluedQcohOn B D.pieces D.unit D.isGluingCocycle (σ := Sum.inr) (h := D.h₁)
   174	    (fun _ => le_rfl) D.cover₁
   175	
   176	/-- The quasi-coherence packaging on the overlap of the pinned charts, from the
   177	restricted chart-0 family (the subordinate-pieces interface). -/
   178	noncomputable instance instQcohOnInf :
   179	    Scheme.QcohOn D.sheaf
   180	      ((relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓ (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁) :=
   181	  gluedQcohOn B D.pieces D.unit D.isGluingCocycle
   182	    (σ := fun j : D.J₀ => Sum.inl j) (h := D.hInf)
   183	    (fun j => D.basicOpen_hInf_le j) D.coverInf
   184	
   185	/-- **The two-cover pair data of the datum's glued sheaf** at the pinned relative chart
   186	coordinates `t₀ᴮ, t₁ᴮ`: overlap-as-basic-open from the landed
   187	`relCover_fiberTwoCover_inf_eq_basicOpen₀/₁`, mutual inverse from the pulled-back
   188	`P1.chartCoord` relation `relFiberCoord_mul`. Its `pair` is the two-lattice pair of the
   189	datum's sheaf that the rigid engine consumes. -/
   190	noncomputable def pairData :
   191	    Scheme.TwoCoverPairData D.sheaf (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
   192	      (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ :=
   193	  gluedPairData B D.pieces D.unit
   194	    (fun _ _ _ => rfl) (fun _ _ _ => rfl)
   195	    (relFiberCoord₀ C B π) (relFiberCoord₁ C B π)
   196	    (relCover_fiberTwoCover_inf_eq_basicOpen₀ C B π)
   197	    (relCover_fiberTwoCover_inf_eq_basicOpen₁ C B π)
   198	    (relFiberCoord_mul C B π)
   199	
   200	end BasicOpenCocycleDatum

   202	end AlgebraicGeometry

    70	/-! ## The complex-form fibre hypothesis from the fibre datum -/
    71	
    72	/-- **The complex-form fibre hypothesis from the fibre datum** (the (1d-ii) second
    73	half): for a `k`-algebra `B'` over the test ring, the vanishing of `H¹` of the
    74	two-lattice pair of the base-changed datum forces the vanishing of the base change of
    75	`H¹` of the pair of the datum: the fibre pair's Čech differential is surjective, the
    76	δ-naturality square (`datumDiffBaseChange`) carries surjectivity to the base-changed
    77	differential, and `H¹(pair) ⊗ B'` is its cokernel by right-exactness. -/
    78	theorem subsingleton_h1_tensor_of_baseChange (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
    79	    (B' : Type u) [CommRing B'] [Algebra k B'] [Algebra B B'] [IsScalarTower k B B']
    80	    (h : Subsingleton (datumPair (D.baseChange B')).H1) :
    81	    Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] B') := by
    82	  -- the fibre pair's differential is surjective
    83	  have himg : (datumPair (D.baseChange B')).imageLattice = ⊤ :=
    84	    Submodule.Quotient.subsingleton_iff.mp h
    85	  have hsurj' : Function.Surjective (datumPair (D.baseChange B')).diff := by
    86	    rw [← LinearMap.range_eq_top, (datumPair (D.baseChange B')).range_diff_eq]
    87	    exact himg
    88	  -- surjectivity transports backward across the δ-naturality square
    89	  have hsq : ∀ a, (D.termBaseChangeInf B').symm ((datumPair (D.baseChange B')).diff a)
    90	      = ((datumPair D).diff.baseChange B') ((D.datumDomBaseChange B').symm a) := by
    91	    intro a
    92	    have hkey := D.datumDiffBaseChange B' ((D.datumDomBaseChange B').symm a)
    93	    rw [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply] at hkey
    94	    rw [← hkey, LinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply]
    95	  have hbc : Function.Surjective ((datumPair D).diff.baseChange B') :=
    96	    RigidEngine.surjective_congr _ _ (D.datumDomBaseChange B').symm
    97	      (D.termBaseChangeInf B').symm hsq hsurj'
    98	  -- the base change of `H¹` is the cokernel of the base-changed differential
    99	  rw [(datumPair D).subsingleton_h1_rTensor_iff B']
   100	  exact Submodule.Quotient.subsingleton_iff.mpr (LinearMap.range_eq_top.mpr hbc)
   101	
   102	/-- The sheaf-level form: `H¹` of the base-changed datum's glued sheaf vanishing
   103	forces the complex-form fibre hypothesis (through `datumH1Equiv` at the fibre
   104	datum). -/
   105	theorem subsingleton_h1_tensor_of_baseChange_sheaf (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
   106	    (B' : Type u) [CommRing B'] [Algebra k B'] [Algebra B B'] [IsScalarTower k B B']
   107	    (h : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (D.baseChange B').sheaf 1)) :
   108	    Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] B') :=
   109	  D.subsingleton_h1_tensor_of_baseChange B'
   110	    ((subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff (D.baseChange B')).mpr h)

   121	/-- **The presentation bridge**: over a field, the datum's glued sheaf is isomorphic
   122	to the glued sheaf of the meromorphic presentation of its canonical subordinated
   123	cocycle (`MeromorphicPresentation.ofCocycle` on the pointed cover by pieces) — the
   124	subordination isomorphism `gluedSheafSubord`.  The presented class is
   125	`E.cechPicClass` by definition. -/
   126	noncomputable def presentationSheafIso (E : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C K π) :
   127	    E.sheaf ≅ (Scheme.MeromorphicPresentation.ofCocycle E.pointedCover
   128	      (gluedSubordCocycle E.isGluingCocycle E.pointedCover E.pieceIndex
   129	        fun _ => le_rfl)).gluedSheaf K :=
   130	  gluedSheafSubord K (σ := E.pieceIndex) (fun _ => le_rfl)
   131	    (fun x y =>
   132	      congrArg Units.val
   133	        (gluedSubordCocycle_evInf E.isGluingCocycle E.pointedCover E.pieceIndex
   134	          (fun _ => le_rfl) x y))
   135	    E.isGluingCocycle
   136	    (fun z => ⟨z, E.pointedCover.mem_opens z⟩)
   137	
   138	/-- **`hfib` in datum sheaf form over a field** (the datum-level face of the W6-full
   139	step (c)+(d) exports): the vanishing of `H¹(𝒪(W))` for any witness divisor `W` of the
   140	datum's Čech Picard class discharges the vanishing of `H¹` of the datum's glued
   141	sheaf. -/
   142	theorem subsingleton_sheaf_h1_of_picClass_eq (E : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C K π)
   143	    {W : (relCurve C K).CurveDivisor}
   144	    (hW : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K W = E.cechPicClass)
   145	    (hvan : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C K).divisorSheaf K W) 1)) :
   146	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule E.sheaf 1) := by
   147	  have hpres : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
   148	      ((Scheme.MeromorphicPresentation.ofCocycle E.pointedCover
   149	        (gluedSubordCocycle E.isGluingCocycle E.pointedCover E.pieceIndex
   150	          fun _ => le_rfl)).gluedSheaf K) 1) :=
   151	    subsingleton_hModule_gluedSheaf_one_of_picClass_eq K _ hW hvan
   152	  exact (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv (presentationSheafIso E) 1).toEquiv.subsingleton_congr.mpr
   153	    hpres
   154	
   155	end Field

   157	/-! ## The seam, closed: the engine's fibre hypothesis from a fibre witness -/
   158	
   159	/-- **The W6-full fibre-restriction seam, closed** (spec-dat-1 (1d-ii) second half):
   160	at a prime `p` of the test ring `B`, a witness divisor `W` of the fibre datum's Čech
   161	Picard class on the fibre curve `C_{κ(p)}` with `H¹(𝒪(W)) = 0` discharges the rigid
   162	engine's complex-form fibre hypothesis `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗[B] κ(p))` — the
   163	`hfib p` clause of `datumRigidEngine` and `datum_subsingleton_pairH1`.
   164	
   165	The fibre curve carries its geometric package by base change
   166	(`Curve.BaseChangeInstances`); the witness is spelled on the product spelling
   167	`(C ⊗ overSpec k κ(p)).left` those instances are keyed on (definitionally
   168	`relCurve C κ(p)`). -/
   169	theorem subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_witness
   170	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   171	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (p : PrimeSpectrum B)
   172	    (hwit : ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k p.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
   173	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass p.asIdeal.ResidueField W
   174	          = (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass
   175	        ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
   176	            ((C ⊗ overSpec k p.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
   177	              p.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)) :
   178	    Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
   179	  obtain ⟨W, hW, hvan⟩ := hwit
   180	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   181	    instIsIntegralBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   182	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   183	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   184	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   185	  haveI : QuasiCompact
   186	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   187	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   188	  refine D.subsingleton_h1_tensor_of_baseChange_sheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField ?_
   189	  exact subsingleton_sheaf_h1_of_picClass_eq (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   190	    hW hvan

     8	/-!
     9	# Canonical pushforward base change for scheme modules
    10	
    11	For a cartesian square of schemes, `canonicalBaseChangeMap` is the Beck--Chevalley mate
    12	
    13	```text
    14	g^* f_* M --> f'_* (g')^* M.
    15	```
    16	
    17	The two coherence theorems identify its pullback followed by the counit with the pullback of
    18	the original counit.  Invertibility is deliberately not asserted here: it is a property of the
    19	module and square, not part of the construction of the canonical map.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	set_option autoImplicit false
    23	
    24	universe u
    25	
    26	open CategoryTheory Limits
    27	
    28	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    29	
    30	/-- The canonical Beck--Chevalley mate for pushforward along a cartesian square. -/
    31	noncomputable def canonicalBaseChangeMap
    32	    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}}
    33	    {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'}
    34	    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) :
    35	    Scheme.Modules.pushforward f ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pullback g ⟶
    36	      Scheme.Modules.pullback g' ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pushforward f' :=
    37	  CategoryTheory.mateEquiv
    38	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f)
    39	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f')
    40	    (((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp f' g) ≪≫
    41	      Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr sq.w.symm ≪≫
    42	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g' f).symm).hom)
    43	
    44	/-- Pulling back the canonical mate and evaluating recovers its defining pullback telescope. -/
    45	theorem canonicalBaseChangeMap_pullback_counit
    46	    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}}
    47	    {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'}
    48	    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) (M : X.Modules) :
    49	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback f').map ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app M) ≫
    50	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f').counit.app
    51	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj M) =
    52	      ((((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp f' g) ≪≫
    53	        Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr sq.w.symm ≪≫
    54	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g' f).symm).hom).app
    55	          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj M)) ≫
    56	        (Scheme.Modules.pullback g').map
    57	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f).counit.app M) := by
    58	  rw [canonicalBaseChangeMap]
    59	  exact CategoryTheory.mateEquiv_counit _ _ _ M
    60	
    61	/-- After cancelling the pullback telescope, the base-changed counit is the pulled-back
    62	original counit. -/
    63	theorem canonicalBaseChangeMap_counit_cancel
    64	    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}}
    65	    {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'}
    66	    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) (M : X.Modules) :
    67	    ((((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp f' g) ≪≫
    68	      Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr sq.w.symm ≪≫
    69	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g' f).symm).inv).app
    70	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj M)) ≫
    71	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f').map ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app M) ≫
    72	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f').counit.app
    73	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj M)) =
    74	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback g').map
    75	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f).counit.app M) := by
    76	  erw [canonicalBaseChangeMap_pullback_counit]
    77	  erw [Iso.inv_hom_id_app_assoc]
    78	  rfl
    79	
    80	end AlgebraicGeometry

    18	
    19	An element of `picDegLayerFunctor` is an etale-plus class, not a chosen line bundle.  The
    20	rank-one route therefore needs an explicit local presentation before it can use the evaluation
    21	map of a line bundle.  `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` records that presentation on an affine
    22	test and ties every piece of data to the input class:
    23	
    24	* a descent-class representative whose plus class is the affine collapse of the input;
    25	* a cocycle datum presenting that same relative Picard class;
    26	* a locally free rank-one `Scheme.Modules` object whose base-ring sheaf is the datum's sheaf;
    27	* invertibility of the canonical native pushforward base-change mate on every cartesian square;
    28	* the cohomological rank-one outputs used by the evaluation construction.
    29	
    30	No existence, openness, or representability assertion is made here.  The first canonical
    31	consumer is `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.evaluation`, the pullback-pushforward counit.
    32	The method `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.h0BaseChange` derives arbitrary affine base change
    33	from the same presentation's `H^1`-vanishing field.  The section bridge at the end identifies
    34	datum `H^0` with native global sections and proves, by the adjunction triangle identity, that
